authors.affiliation: NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, Tokyo, Japan
authors.bio: Nagato Narita received B.E., M.E., and Ph.D. degrees in electrical engineering from Waseda University, Tokyo, Japan, in 1983, 1985, and 1996, respectively. He joined NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corporation) in 1985. Since 1988, he has been with the Science and Technical Research Laboratories of NHK. His research interest has been in the field of evaluation of picture quality. Currently he is engaged in research and development of future television systems. — Narita is a member of the Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers of Japan and the Institute of Television Engineers of Japan.
authors.name: Nagato Narita

authors.affiliation: NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, Tokyo, Japan
authors.bio: Yakio Sugiura received the B.E. degree in electrical engineering from Tokyo Denki University, Tokyo, Japan, in 1963 and the Ph.D. degree in electronic engineering from the University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan, in 1995. — Sugiura joined NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corp.) in 1958. Since then he has been with the Science and Technical Research Laboratories of NHK, where he is engaged in research on advanced television systems. Presently Sugiura is a senior research engineer of Three Dimensional Audio-Visual Systems Research Division. — Sugiura is a member of the Institute of Television Engineers of Japan, the Optical Society of Japan, and the Motion Picture and Television Engineering Society of Japan.
authors.name: Yukio Sugiura

authors.affiliation: NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, Tokyo, Japan
authors.bio: Ichiro Yuyama received B.E. and Ph.D. degrees in electronic engineering from the University of Tokyo, in 1970 and 1991, respectively. — Yuyama joined NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corp.) in 1970. He then spent 1973-74 at the CBS Technology Center in Stamford, Conn. Since 1975, he has been with the Science and Technical Research Laboratories of NHK, where he was engaged in research and development of HDTV and where he headed an EDTV project from 1985 to 1989. He is presently a director of the Three Dimensional Audio-Visual Systems Research Division. — Yuyama is a member of SMPTE, the Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers of Japan, the Institute of Television Engineers of Japan, the Motion Picture and Television Engineering Society of Japan, the Acoustical Society of Japan, and the Virtual Reality Society of Japan.
authors.name: Ichiro Yuyama
